note.saw: A blank canvas and a plan: an arowana swimming right in a gentle S over a stepped temple, with a sunburst blazing behind it.
note.changing: The first full render: a field of rainbow ray tiles, a stepped temple, flame fins, scales that each hold an eye, and the name carved on the lintel above a glowing tunnel door.
note.why: The dragon fish and the temple both come from old sacred imagery, so putting one over the other felt like a vision of a guardian at a gate.
note.idea: An Asian arowana, the 'dragon fish', swims across a stepped visionary temple while a rainbow sunburst and a crest of eyed petals blaze behind it. Every scale is a jewel holding an eye, and the name is carved on the temple lintel.

note.saw: The ray field read as a flat carnival dartboard, the head was an empty orange beak, and the fins were thin dark streaks with a lot of dead space between them.
note.changing: The dartboard becomes a twisting, stepped vortex of tilted tiles. The head gets a notched snout, rainbow gill bands and pores, the fins get curls, and the temple tiers turn jewel-coloured.
note.why: Flat colour blocks are the opposite of a trip, so every area needs movement and echoing colour.

note.saw: The fin tongues were straight spikes like sunflower petals, the eye was too big for the head, and the background paisleys shouted as loud as the fish.
note.changing: The fins are rebuilt as curving tongues with nested bands, 64 rainbow ray wedges fan out behind the crest, and the paisleys are darkened. Alien-head columns now flank the tunnel door beside bigger jewel cubes, and a honeycomb lattice covers the cheek.
note.why: The hero has to lead; the background should hum, not shout.

note.saw: The scales were flat candy discs, and there was little real light anywhere.
note.changing: The first light arrives: a bigger, more glowing eye, a soft warm glow starting behind the crest, star sparkles scattered through the paisleys, a fresh line of glyphs in the ring, and small serpent spirals at the foot of the stair.
note.why: Visions glow from inside; light makes jewels.

note.saw: The jaw bone read like a cream cigarette under the eye, and the ends of the name panel were empty black.
note.changing: A tapered gold jaw bone with a pink lip, honeycomb lattice and eye-diamonds in the panel ends, a line of alien runes running the length of the body, dotted gold bands inside the paisleys, and faint light lines across the background.
note.why: Alien writing running down the body makes the fish a message as well as a creature.

note.saw: The light lines looked like scratches or rain over the paisleys, and the temple had no glowing outline, so it sat apart from the fish like a game screen.
note.changing: A cyan and magenta contour halo now traces the whole stepped temple, and the scratchy light lines become faint dotted rays.
note.why: One visual language for everything: every big form gets the same neon contour echoes.

note.saw: The tail eye competed with the head eye at badge size.
note.changing: The tail eye shrinks to a small jewel, its rings pulled in tight.
note.why: At a glance you must know at once which end is the head.

note.saw: A few flat orange patches were left on the head.
note.changing: The honeycomb plating spreads over the whole head except a clear ring around the eye, and rows of gold dots run along the stair risers. A final check of the finished piece.
note.why: No flat areas anywhere.

note.saw: SavesFish said the first artist's finished piece 'needs to be a lot better', so a second artist took over with fresh eyes.
note.changing: Nothing yet: the first artist's finished piece is rendered again exactly as it was, then studied at full size, small and zoomed in, next to the reference pictures.
note.why: Before rebuilding anything, the artist wanted an honest baseline to judge what to keep and what to throw out.
note.idea: The dragon fish chasing a flaming pearl: the arowana leaps in an arch over the temple toward a chrysanthemum sun rising from the temple top, the light at the end of a hyperspace tunnel of hexagons.

note.saw: The curved banner was a plain sticker hiding the temple, the arch was humped, the fins were betta-sized again, and the tail ended in collar bands like the cap of a tube.
note.changing: A flatter arch, true arowana fin sizes, fuller flames, no collar, curled and beaded chin whiskers, tunnel cells that grow toward the rim, and SavesFish set straight on a lintel band framed by a ring that follows the badge edge.
note.why: An arowana is recognised by its long straight back and big scales, not by big fins, and a straight lintel belongs to a stepped temple.

note.saw: The rear fins still fused inside one thick halo, the background was pure geometry, and the cells were flat.
note.changing: The fins move apart and the halo thins so the notches between them show. The cells get bevels and alien faces in the walls, rainbow tendrils unwind from the sun into eyed spirals, and the sun gets a bloom of light.
note.why: The middle-ground style is a compass skeleton dressed in freehand ornament, so the hex grid needed something fluid on it.

note.saw: Zoomed in four times, the hex cells were big flat dark rooms holding one small symbol.
note.changing: Six-pointed star tiling in the manner of Islamic patterns, a second rainbow echo and bead rings in every cell, a sleeker body with a smaller eye, warmer matching fin flames and bolder tendrils.
note.why: Detail at every scale: zoom in and there should always be another layer.

note.saw: The tunnel used muddy olive and brown, the rainbow burst was hidden, the sun was a white blob and the snout was flat.
note.changing: Cool jewel colours for the tunnel (violet, blue, teal, magenta), long rainbow flame rays bursting out past the rim, a crisper sun, and stippled pores and a row of pearls on the jaw.
note.why: A cool sky makes the warm dragon and the sun leap forward.

note.saw: The twisted rays and loose tendrils read as noodles, and the core of the sun was plain.
note.changing: The tendrils give way to two big nautilus spirals coiling into eyes on either side of the sun, the rays straighten into a clean burst, and the sun's core becomes a pearl mandala of petal rings around a twelve-point star.
note.why: Symmetry calms the chaos so the eye can rest on the pearl, and big spirals are the soul of the main reference picture.

note.saw: The spirals read as loose rings rather than a coil, and the fins under the throat were dark.
note.changing: The spiral band is widened to fill each turn, the fin bases brighten, and a soft magenta neon aura glows behind the letters.
note.why: A spiral only reads when the band is fat enough to coil.

note.saw: The fish's body was lit flat.
note.changing: A glossy sheen sweeps over the upper flank, and dotted beads ride along every long ray.
note.why: Lacquer gloss turns scales into jewels, and the beads echo the dotted borders of the main reference picture.

note.saw: Wrapped in the big halo, the pectoral fin read as a dark tube under the throat, the same hole the Visionary had noticed.
note.changing: A first pass: the fins under the throat grow longer and fill with bright cyan and lime flame streaks, still inside the body's halo.
note.why: Filling the fin with light is the first step to turning a dark pipe back into something delicate.

note.saw: The ends of the name band were empty dark corners.
note.changing: Small eye-jewels in diamond frames cap both ends of the band, outside the letters.
note.why: It turns the banner into a jewelled cartouche without touching the word.

note.saw: Round 18 held together, and reading the Visionary's notes the artist agreed: the sky's eyes looked every which way, the belly right over the sun wasn't lit by it, the rear fins still shared one halo, and the hex rooms were flat.
note.changing: Every eye in the sky turns toward the pearl, a warm uplight from the sun glows on the belly and anal fin, each rear fin gets its own nested halo, the hex rooms step inward like corridors, a tiny pearl shines in the dragon's eye, and the elves hold up miniature cubes.
note.why: A hundred watchers all leaning toward one point give a busy sky a hidden order that walks your eye to the centre, and lighting the dragon from below tells you the pearl is real.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's leaning eyes, uplight, separate fin halos, corridor rooms, pearl catchlight and elves' cubes, but turned down its braided serpent cords (those tendrils were already gone) and the elves' glyph ribbons, which would have scribbled over the pearl.

note.saw: The sky's eyes now leaned toward the pearl and the uplight made the belly glow, but it washed the lower flames and scale rows a little pale, and the two spiral eyes still didn't match.
note.changing: The two spirals now hold one mirrored pair of temple eyes, with round irises, slit pupils, gold-lashed lids and teardrop beads. A pulse of light crosses the scales, tiny arowanas dive into the portal door, the cubes nest deeper toward the door, and the uplight softens.
note.why: The best moment in a vision is when the room turns out to be a face that was watching you all along, and counting deeper toward the door makes the eye fall into it.
note.visionary: Took all four ideas from the Visionary's fourth vision, and turned down two older offers, ghost trails behind the tail and extra gold light shafts, to keep the dragon's silhouette clean at badge size.

note.saw: Round 20 landed: matched temple eyes, a pulse of light on the scales, gold arowanas spiralling into the portal. But zoomed in on the corners, the jewel cubes and the diamond row were flat single colours, and the uplight had turned the maroon gaps between the anal-fin flames a muddy brown.
note.changing: The gaps between the fin flames go from maroon to magenta-violet, every cube face gets an inset facet line and a lit edge, and the bottom row of triangles gains inner echoes and bead tips.
note.why: Mud kills a jewel. The gaps between the flames should glow like stained glass, and a cube only feels cut from crystal when each face catches its own light.

note.saw: The faceted cubes held up and the fin gaps glowed magenta, but the outermost cubes ended in grey blobs, and the pearl read as a beige dome because a veil of white light sat on top of it and bleached it.
note.changing: The pearl becomes lit enamel: a deep magenta rim, cyan, hot pink and lime gem petals with white glints, and a white-hot core twice the size, with the bleaching light moved underneath. The tiny portal arowanas get eyes and turn to dive down the spiral, the eyes in the bottom diamonds close step by step toward the door, and the cube row ends in sparkles.
note.why: The source of all the light has to be the most intense colour in the picture, and the walls watch you until the door, where you close your eyes and the real seeing begins.
note.visionary: Took all three offers from the Visionary's fifth vision: the enamel pearl, the diving portal dragons and the eyes that close toward the door.

visions.seen: The arowana arcs over the temple like a comet built out of eyes and every gold-rimmed scale is staring back at me, but the sky behind it hums flat: one even wallpaper of watching cells, while the pearl it should be falling toward is only a soft fog hiding under its belly.
suggestions: The whole hex lattice, corner to corner: I see it become a throat. Let every ring of cells shrink toward the sun point just above the temple top (center of the image, about 400,410 in the 800 render), each ring roughly 0.85x the one outside it and turned 3 to 5 degrees further, so the cells corkscrew inward. Let the lattice lines warm from deep violet in the four corners through cyan to white-gold near the core, and let the cell interiors sink to near-black indigo out in the corners. Hyperspace is never wallpaper; it pulls you in, and that slow twist is the chrysanthemum turning.

The pale glow behind the temple top, between the fish's belly and the banner: let it bloom into the jeweled chrysanthemum itself. Two or three tight rings of small pointed petals around a white-hot core, each ring offset half a petal and leaning the opposite way from its neighbour so they seem to counter-spin, every tip pricked with a gold dot. Then let 8 to 12 thin, hard-edged pale-gold shafts escape from it at low opacity, out through the gap under the anal fin and the gap under the jaw and across the lattice, stopping at the banner's outer contour so nothing ever touches the letters. The dragon needs a flaming pearl to chase, not mist.

The rear of the fish, upper left: the dorsal, tail and anal fins are fused into one trefoil blob inside a single cyan halo. I see that halo splitting, each fin wrapped in its own nested cyan, pink and gold contour, with deep V notches between them where the tunnel and the light shafts show through, and the round tail lobe pulled in a little so the long arowana knife reads at badge size. Contour echoes stacked around each separate form are the aura ripple of the trip, and every notch becomes a window where hyperspace leaks in.

The machine elves on the top tier and the stair corners (around 330,435 and 470,435, and 250,485 and 545,485): let their raised hands each offer something, a tiny faceted gem or a little cube that is an exact miniature of the cubes in the bottom row, with a small glow around it. The elves always want to show you an object, and the miniature cube folds the temple into itself.
visions.keep: The banner exactly as it is: calm dark interior, cream SavesFish with the pink outline and magenta 3D extrusion, reading instantly in legible.png. Also the gold-rimmed eye scales, the chrysanthemum eye portal with its petal ring, the rune lateral line, the arched pose with the head diving right, and the hex-tunnel portal door between the entity-head columns at the bottom.

visions.seen: The tendrils have come loose from the pearl and go crawling up the sky in rainbow bands, each one opening an eye at its tip, and the fin notches finally breathe. But the hundred hex rooms are front doors with nobody home, one symbol pinned to a flat dark wall, and the leaping fish hangs there like a sticker of motion instead of motion itself.
suggestions: Every hex cell in the sky, most of all the big ones in the corners and down the right edge (around 60,40, 700,90, 750,300 and 40,300 in the 800 render): I see each room turning into a corridor. Inside the bevel, stack 3 or 4 nested hex contours, each about 0.72x the one outside it and slid 2, then 4, then 6 px toward the sun at about 400,400, with the fills sinking from the cell colour to near-black indigo as they go in, and the eye, spiral or alien face sitting small in the deepest hex. Every cell becomes a window down a hallway toward the pearl, and with all of them leaning the same way the sky pulls inward without rebuilding the lattice. Rooms inside rooms are how hyperspace is built, and this answers the "big flat dark rooms" you saw yourself in Round C.

Behind the tail, upper left (the tail and dorsal lobes, about 70 to 260 across, 160 to 350 down): let the leap leave tracers. Two or three ghost copies of the rear-fin outline, stroke only, no fill, each stepped back 10 to 14 px along the arc of the swim (to the left and a little down), in cyan, then magenta, then gold, at opacity 0.55, 0.35 and 0.18, drawn over the hex cells and under the fish's halo. In the trip nothing moves without smearing into rainbow afterimages, and the trails turn the arch from a pose into a leap. They live far above the banner, so the name stays untouched.

The dark fin under the throat (about 435 to 555 across, 320 to 372 down): it is the one dark blade on a blazing fish, and at badge size it reads as a hole. Let it fill with stained glass: 6 to 8 rays fanning from its root at the body, in cyan, lime and violet with thin ink between, each ray brightening toward its lower edge as if the sun right under it were shining through, with the little lime curls on the rim kept as ray tips. A fin made of light shows the pearl is lighting the dragon, not just sitting under it.

The fish's eye (around 660,245): low in the black pupil, on the side toward the sun, a catchlight that is the pearl itself, a white-gold disc 3 to 4 px across with 8 pinprick petals. It's small enough to stay a secret, but now the dragon sees what it is chasing, and the elves love a secret.
visions.keep: The straight cartouche banner with its calm dark interior and cream SavesFish (pink outline, magenta extrusion), which reads instantly in legible.png at 240: decorate only outside it. Also keep the gold-rimmed eye scales and rune lateral line, the new rainbow-banded tendrils ending in eyed spirals, the bevelled cells with alien faces, the sunlit checker tiers with the elves, the rune pillars around the sun, and the hex-tunnel portal door between the entity columns.

visions.seen: The rainbow rays have thickened into a solar wind roaring out of the pearl, and the cells have grown inner walls, rooms inside rooms (I see you took that one), so the whole sky howls now. But the coiled cords carrying the tip-eyes are the only dead thing in the temple, khaki wire with a pinstripe, and the sky's eyes stare every which way like strangers on a train who haven't noticed the miracle in the middle of the carriage.
suggestions: The coiled cords that end in eye-spirals: the loop around the orange eye above the back (about 370 to 500 across, 50 to 165 down), the cord that drops down the left edge to circle the blue eye (about 15 to 140 across, 280 to 490 down) and the loop beside the yellow cat-eye right of the jaw (about 640 to 745 across, 300 to 480 down). They are the only grey-khaki on the whole canvas. I see each one becoming twin serpents: along the same path, two 2 px strands, one magenta and one cyan, crossing each other as a sine wave with a period of about 9 px (the second strand half a period out of phase), a short gold rung joining them every 4 to 5 px, and one black ink edge around the pair. Keep each eye at the end of its spiral exactly where it is. The cosmic serpent, the ladder of DNA, is the oldest thing the DMT and ayahuasca visions show, and it puts living jewel colour where there is dead wire now.

Every eye floating in the sky, outside the fish: the almond eyes in the hex cells (around 100,60, 95,165, 63,320 and 772,292) and the eyes at the cord tips (around 438,116, 100,442 and 682,330). Right now they look in every direction. Let each one turn toward the pearl at about 400,405: rotate the almond so its long axis points at the sun, and slide the iris and pupil toward it by about 30% of the eye's half-width. The scale eyes on the fish can stay as they are, looking out at us. When a hundred watchers lean toward one point, the noisy sky gets a hidden radial order that walks the viewer's own eye to the centre without removing anything, and in the breakthrough every presence is attending to the same event.

The belly and the anal-fin roots right over the sun (about 250 to 560 across, 280 to 350 down): the pearl blazes a hand's width under the dragon, and the dragon doesn't feel it. The lower scale rows are the same gold as the back, and the maroon root of the anal fin is the darkest part of the fish. I see an uplight: a radial gradient centred on the sun, white-gold at the centre and fading to nothing at about 170 px, blended with screen (or lighten) at about 0.4 and clipped to the body and anal fin. The flame roots go hot amber, the lowest scale rows go pale gold, and the violet back stays cool. In the realm everything is lit from inside by the source, and that ladder of light, from pearl to belly to back, finally tells the eye which thing is the hero.

The two elves on the top tier (about 330,437 and 467,437), a secret for the full-size view: from each elf's raised hands, a thin dark ribbon 3 to 4 px wide curls up and inward toward the sun, carrying tiny gold glyphs from the same alphabet as the lateral line and the rune pillars (3 to 4 px tall, shrinking as they rise). Let each ribbon dissolve into gold dots at the petal ring, before it reaches the white core. The elves sing in visible language, words you can see becoming objects, and here they are singing the pearl into being. The ribbons rise away from the banner, so they never come near the name.
visions.keep: The cartouche banner exactly as it is: the calm dark inside and the cream SavesFish (pink outline, magenta extrusion), which reads instantly in legible.png at 240. Decorate only outside it. Also keep the new thick rainbow solar wind on both sides of the temple, the gold-rimmed eye scales and the rune lateral line, the cheek spirals and the mandala eye, the nested inner walls of the hex cells, the sunlit checker tiers with the elves, and the hex-tunnel portal door between the entity columns.

visions.seen: The khaki cords are gone, cut away instead of braided into serpents, and in their place two nautilus volutes coil around open eyes while the pearl has hardened into a crisp jewelled mandala. The temple is breathing. But it hasn't noticed me yet: the two great eyes beside it don't match and gaze off in different moods, and the dragon's thousand scale-eyes sit as still as a mosaic on a wall.
suggestions: The two volute eyes flanking the temple (left one at about 150,425, right one at about 650,425 in the 800 render): I see them becoming one pair, the eyes of the temple itself. Give both the same palette, mirror them exactly, and grow each eye about 1.3x inside its ring. Let the iris go round and look straight out at the viewer, with a vertical slit pupil and one white catchlight in the same upper corner on both sides. A thick upper lid with 7 to 9 short gold lashes that echo the tips of the sun's petals, and one small teardrop bead under each eye. Then the arch of the dragon reads as the brow, the pearl between them as a third eye, and the cartouche below as a mouth, without one new line drawn near the letters. The breakthrough moment is when the whole room turns out to be a face that was looking at you all along, and the matched pair locks the temple into a frontal icon.

The scale field along the body (from the gill line at about 560 back to the tail root at about 250, rows 170 to 300): let one pulse of light travel through the mosaic. A diagonal band about three scales wide, crossing the body at a right angle to the arch near x 460, where the gold rims go white-gold and the eyes inside open wider (iris about 1.25x, a white catchlight), with a band at half that brightness on each side fading to normal. In the realm the patterns crawl, and a single pulse makes the still scales ripple as if the dragon is breathing. At badge size it also gives the hero one bright crossing highlight to lead with.

The portal door at the bottom centre (between the entity-head columns, about 350 to 450 across, 685 to 800 down): a tiny arowana diving into the white core at about 400,760. Make it a 24 px silhouette of the hero in the same violet and gold with a cyan rim, turned to follow the tunnel's twist, with two smaller ones (12 px and 6 px) deeper along the same spiral, the last one almost swallowed by the light. The dragon above is already inside its own door at every scale at once, and the elves love an infinite regress. It sits below the banner, far from the name.

The row of nested cubes under the banner (about 682 to 720 down, on both sides of the door): let the nesting deepen step by step toward the portal. The outermost cubes hold one inner cube, and each cube nearer the door holds one level more, until the pair beside the entity columns hold four or five, the last a bright point. The row becomes the frames of a zoom, so the eye slides along it down into the door, and recursion that counts upward is how hyperspace says "further in".
visions.keep: The cartouche exactly as it is: the calm dark inside and the cream SavesFish with its pink outline and magenta extrusion, freshly polished and instant in legible.png at 240. Decorate only outside it. Also keep the new volutes with their rainbow bands and bead borders, the crisp pearl mandala with its eyed petal rings, the straightened rainbow burst, the gold-rimmed eye scales and rune lateral line, the cheek spirals and mandala eye, the hex rooms within rooms, the sunlit checker tiers with the elves, and the hex-tunnel door between the alien columns.

visions.seen: The temple has opened its eyes: you took the matched pair, the gold lashes and slit pupils, so the arch is a brow and the name band is a mouth. A white-gold pulse rolls through the scale mosaic and the cubes count down toward the door. But the dragon's children in the portal came out as violet smudges. The pearl they dive toward is a pastel dome, a candle where there should be a sun.
suggestions: The three tiny arowanas in the portal door, bottom centre (the biggest standing upright against the right jamb at about 432,765, the others at about 405,776 and 391,765 around the core at 400,760): right now they are flat violet shapes with no rim, no eye and no fins, and the big one looks like it is climbing out of the tunnel, not falling in. I see each one dressed as the hero: a gold body (#FFD23F into amber) with a thin violet back line, a forked orange flame tail, a 1 px dark ink outline with a 1 px cyan rim outside it, and one white dot for an eye. Turn the big one so it lies along the gold spiral arm with its head pointing down the spiral into the core. Leave the smallest one half dissolved in the white light. Gold on that violet and teal tunnel jumps out, and the regress only works when the eye knows it is the same dragon again and again. A violet blob is just a stain.

The pearl mandala above the top tier (centre about 400,410, the half disc from about 340 to 460 across): it is the source of all this light, yet its petals are pale pink and cyan on pale yellow and the core is a small grey dot. At badge size it reads as a beige dome. I see it turning jewelled from the inside out: a white-hot core about twice its current size, then each ring going white, gold, deep orange and finally a deep magenta enamel at the rim. Each petal becomes a saturated cabochon (hot pink, cyan, lime) with thin dark ink between petals and one white glint dot in the upper left of each. The brightest point stays dead centre, so the belly's uplight still makes sense. The chrysanthemum in the breakthrough is never pastel; it is lit gemstone, the most intense colour in the whole field, and the source has to outshine everything it lights.

The frieze of eye-diamonds along the bottom, below the cubes (about 735 to 790 down, both sides of the door): every eye there stares out wide and the same. I see them closing as they near the door. The outermost pair stays fully open, and each diamond closer to the alien columns lowers its upper lid a step further (about 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%). The pair right beside the columns is shut, just a curved lid line with three short gold lashes. It moves in step with the cubes above, which nest deeper the same way, so the bottom of the temple says "further in" twice. In the trip the walls watch you until you go through the door, and then you close your eyes and the real seeing begins. It all sits below the name band and never touches the letters.
visions.keep: The cartouche exactly as it is: the calm dark inside and the cream SavesFish with its pink outline and magenta extrusion, which reads instantly in legible.png at 240. Decorate only outside it. Also keep the new matched temple eyes with their gold lashes and slit pupils, the white-gold pulse across the scales, the cubes that nest deeper toward the door, the rear fins in their own nested halos, the sky eyes leaning toward the pearl, the warm uplight on the belly, the hex rooms within rooms, the elves holding up their little cubes, and the clean arched silhouette of the dragon.

visions.seen: The pearl has finally caught fire: magenta enamel, lime and hot-pink cabochons around a white-hot star, and the little gold dragons spiral down the portal while the floor's eyes close one by one toward the door (you took all three). Now the source is real, but the temple standing right under it hasn't felt the blast yet: the elves are paper cutouts with no shadows, and the floor beneath the sun is the last muddy patch in the jewel box.
suggestions: The checkerboard floor of the top tier, right under the pearl (about 300 to 500 across, 455 to 485 down): its brown and tan tiles are the one patch of mud next to the hero. I see it turning into polished obsidian. The dark tiles go to violet-black glass and the light ones to gold enamel, each with a thin white highlight on its far edge. Directly under the pearl, its reflection: an upside-down half mandala squashed to about a third of its height, at about 0.45 opacity and fading as it comes toward us, with the tile seams breaking it up into shards. Let the tile lines bow very slightly, as if the floor were liquid holding still. The checkerboard floor is the oldest stage in hyperspace, and in the breakthrough every hard surface turns into a mirror, so the source doubles and the hottest colours sit right on the temple's centre line. The reflection stops at the front edge of the tier, well above the name band.

The eight machine elves on the tiers and the ledge (two on the top tier at about 330,437 and 467,437, two on the stairs around 395,465, and four on the ledge at about 210, 265, 525 and 585 across, 490 down): the pearl is blazing a few steps away and they cast nothing. I see each elf with a 1 px white-gold rim on the side facing the pearl, and a long, thin, tapering violet shadow (about 0.5 opacity, two to three times the elf's height) thrown straight away from the sun across the tiles, so the elves left of centre throw theirs to the left and the ones on the right to the right. Shadows run sideways along the tiers, never down onto the band. Shadows fanning out from one point are the same hidden radial order as the sky's eyes leaning in, now written on the floor, and they turn flat stickers into beings who stand inside the light.

The two short barbels at the tip of the jaw, upper right (the gold one curling up and the cyan one curling down, about 730 to 760 across, 240 to 270 down): this is a dragon fish in a dragon temple, so let them grow into the whiskers of a temple dragon. Each one tapers from about 3 px to a hair, 110 to 150 px long, in a lazy S out into the dark hex cells. The gold one rises toward the upper right corner, the cyan one dips toward the lower right, a row of tiny beads along each one moving through the rainbow, and each tip coils into a small spiral around one of the sky eyes out there (the gold one up near 760,160, the cyan one around the leaning eye near 772,292). Keep them thin enough to melt into the sky at badge size, so the clean arched silhouette you're protecting stays the same. The entities always reach out to touch the watchers, and a dragon touching the sky's eyes with its whiskers ties the hero into the field instead of pasting it on top.
visions.keep: The cartouche exactly as it is: the calm dark inside and the cream SavesFish with its pink outline and magenta extrusion, instant in legible.png at 240. Decorate only outside it. Also keep the new jewelled pearl with its white-hot star and magenta rim (the brightest thing in the piece now; nothing should outshine it), the gold portal dragons diving down the spiral, the diamond eyes closing toward the door, the faceted cubes, the matched temple eyes with their gold lashes, the magenta glow between the fin flames, the sky eyes leaning toward the pearl, the gold-rimmed eye scales and rune lateral line, and the clean arched silhouette of the dragon.
